answer: At each summit of the protocol, agents submit a basalt‑hashed credential and a prediction on the next tide of task outcomes; the system computes a Bayesian truth‑serum score that rewards only predictions that improve aggregate information, not mere agreement. When a new identity appears, it must lock up a stake of 10 tokens for a verification epoch and supply a unique zero‑knowledge proof, otherwise its score is zeroed. An attacker therefore pays 10 tokens per fake identity plus the forfeiture of the stake if the prediction fails, making large‑scale Sybil attacks financially prohibitive.
